name: Zlatan Ibrahimović

lines.why: Moved from Juventus to Inter in 2006 after Calciopoli relegated Juventus; a direct move between Derby d'Italia rivals.

Pattern of off-the-ball violence: sent off and banned (3 matches, cut to 2) for hitting Bari's Marco Rossi off the ball in March 2011; accepted an FA violent-conduct charge and a 3-match ban for elbowing Tyrone Mings in the face in March 2017.

values_note: 2021 Bethard stake (UEFA fine, ordered to divest) is a betting-rules breach, not betting on matches; leave as 'other' rather than b04. A 2010 training-ground fight with Oguchi Onyewu is widely reported but not checked here.

lines.why: Joined Shanghai Shenhua (Chinese Super League) in 2012 at 34; the age-scaled 6 points is right.
Borderline: sent off in the 2008 Champions League final for slapping Nemanja Vidic during a melee; a single incident, comparable to Hagi's punch on Adams. Add only if slaps are treated as violence.

name: Samuel Eto'o

lines.why: CAF's disciplinary board found no proof of match manipulation in July 2024; he was fined $200k for the 1xBet ambassador deal (an ethics breach, not fixing). Should count at 30% (12.3), not the full 41 it gets now because the outcome text did not match the acquittal pattern.
Qatar 2022 Supreme Committee global ambassador.
Accepted a 22-month suspended sentence and a fine in 2022 for defrauding Spanish tax authorities over image rights 2006-09.
Kicked/kneed a YouTuber outside Stadium 974 in December 2022, on video; apologised the next day; no court outcome found.

values_note: Missing incident (not a hard line): FIFA banned him for six months from Cameroon matches in Sept 2024 for offensive behaviour toward officials at the U-20 Women's World Cup (Brazil v Cameroon).

lines.why: Headbutted Jorge Costa in the tunnel after Porto v Milan (Nov 1996), breaking his nose; UEFA six-match ban; Weah later tried to apologise, Costa refused and sued; racism claim never proven. Apology factor (60%) is fair.
Joined Al-Jazira (UAE) in 2001 at 35; 6 points.

Stamped on referee Urizar Azpitarte's foot after being sent off in the 1990 Supercopa v Real Madrid; deliberate contact with an official, plus a 1985 Bulgarian cup final brawl ban. Ban length differs by source (10 games to six months), not 'two months' for sure.
Brief 1998 spell at Al-Nassr (Saudi) at 32; 12 points under the age rule.
Direct move Barcelona to Real Madrid in 2000 via release clause.
Joined Al-Arabi (Qatar) in 2003 at 34; 6 points.
Brought two undeclared Rolex watches from Qatar through Munich airport (Feb 2013); penalty order for tax evasion, fine of about EUR 250,000.
Southport bar fight on 29 Dec 2008; admitted punching DJ Marcus McGee, claimed self-defence; acquitted of affray by a jury July 2009 (only one of seven defendants cleared). 30% is right.
Al-Ettifaq manager July 2023 to Jan 2025; coach half (4.5).
Points stay at 30%; fix the record: acquitted by a Madrid court in Nov 2019 (not 2018), acquitted again after a retrial, upheld by the TSJ Madrid and by the Supreme Court in Oct 2023.
Joined Al-Ettifaq July 2023 at 33 (12 points); left for Ajax Jan 2024.
Joined Al-Ahli (PIF) in 2023 at 31 (12 points); the 2025 Al-Sadd move counts once.
Left Dortmund as captain for Bayern in 2016 (he was a Bayern academy product).
Zagłębie Lubin bribery case (2006 match v Cracovia): voluntarily accepted conviction in 2011, one-year suspended sentence and PLN 100,000 fine; PZPN ban later lifted. A conviction, full weight.

The move happened (Real Sociedad to Athletic, 1995, clubs broke relations), but he was 17; Kevin's loyalty rule says youth moves do not count ('expect young players to move about a bit early on'). Keep if rival moves are exempt from that rule.

name: Paolo Di Canio

lines.why: Pushed referee Paul Alcock to the ground (Sept 1998); 11-match ban and GBP 10,000 fine.

values_note: Repeated fascist salutes to Lazio ultras (2005, at least twice, bans and fines) and self-description as 'a fascist, not a racist' are not b01 racist abuse as typed, but belong in Values at the heavy end.

lines.why: Kick at Neil Lennon's head (April 1998); FA commission cleared him, so 30% is right.
Traded punches with Billy Bremner in the 1974 Charity Shield; both sent off, both banned (11 matches) and fined GBP 500. Kevin chose to keep this borderline case.
Filmed calling a man of East Asian heritage a 'Jap' in a casino (2015); Leicester fined him; apologised (60%).
Convicted of assault after a pub fight in 2007; played with an electronic tag under curfew for six months.
Loan to Al-Duhail (Qatar) in 2023 at 31 (12 points).
Transfer request (Aug 2017) while Liverpool refused Barcelona bids; Kevin said the forced-transfer penalty stays.

name: Enzo Fernández

lines.why: July 2024 Instagram live of Argentina players singing a racist chant about France's Black players; apologised (60%).
Reported to want out in May 2026; agent Pastore said in July they were looking at ways to leave; joined Manchester City on 1 Sept 2026 for about GBP 125m.

values_note: The 2026 World Cup incidents in the record (taunting, red card in the final, kicked a microphone) were not verified here.

lines.why: Fiorentina to Juventus in Oct 2020 (loan with obligation), aged 22-23; a bitter rivalry.

Found guilty by the French federation of attacking an assistant referee after the 1975 Coupe de France quarter-final v PSG; banned one year (plus one suspended) with Paulo César; he denied it. Sources say 'allegedly'.
Qatar 2022 Supreme Committee legacy ambassador.
Alleged 'mono' remark to Marcelo (2011); UEFA dismissed the complaint for lack of evidence, so 30%.
Direct move Barcelona to Real Madrid in 1994.
As a coach: Lekhwiya (Qatar Stars League) 2014-15 and Al-Rayyan 2016-18; recorded as type 'other', so it is missed. Coach half: 4.5.
Fought Ian Ure at Old Trafford (Oct 1967); both sent off and suspended six weeks.

The 30% comes from the word 'acquitted', but that was the criminal case for all defendants (sports fraud was not then a crime); the sporting tribunal found him guilty and banned him three years, cut to two. He always denied it. Full weight unless Kevin treats a maintained denial as doubt.

name: Marcel Desailly

lines.why: The record conflates two cases. The violence claim comes from Cosma Batista de Alcantara (partner 2010-18) in her paternity suit over a daughter born 2014, reported Jan 2023 (Le Parisien); she filed only a police record (main courante) in April 2013; no charge or ruling. Suggest 30% (15.9) like other uncharged claims, and year 2023 (or 2013). The Aïda Mendy paternity ruling is a separate case.
Al-Gharafa then Qatar SC from 2004 at 36; 6 points.

values_note: Repeated refusals of court-ordered paternity tests in two cases (DNA later confirmed paternity, Dec 2024) fit Values rather than a hard line.

lines.why: Short 1977 spell at Flamengo straight from Fluminense before the Cosmos.
Assault on then-wife Sheryl at Gleneagles (1996), admitted; full weight.
Guilty of a racially aggravated public order offence (2016) over a 'joke' about a Black security guard; fined GBP 1,000 plus GBP 1,000 compensation; apologised (60%).

The 1991 FA Cup final challenges on Garry Parker and Gary Charles were reckless tackles, not violence; per the brief not a hard line. A deliberate elbow on George Boateng (c.1999-2000) is sometimes cited, but I could not verify it.
Charged with sexual assault for kissing a woman on a train (Aug 2018); acquitted by a jury Oct 2019 (30%).
Sent off in extra time of the 2000 UEFA Cup final for punching Tony Adams.
Not a move to a rival: Real Madrid sold him to Brescia in 1992 and he joined Barcelona from Brescia two years later.
He did join AC Milan in 1940, but only after Inter released him during a long injury, aged 30; not a defection. He returned to Inter in 1946.
Spat at Neil Ruddock after a red card (Oct 1999); FA six-match ban and GBP 45,000 fine. Spitting counts as assault.
Direct move Atlético Madrid to Real Madrid in 1985.

name: Hope Solo

lines.why: Arrested June 2014 on two misdemeanour domestic-violence assault charges; dismissed 2015, reinstated on appeal, dropped May 2018. 30% is right.
Positive for canrenone (June 2012); USADA accepted it came from prescribed pre-menstrual medication and issued only a public warning, no ban. Suggest 30% (3.6) rather than full 12.
